say: Blades stay sheathed, tabs get paid, and I didn't see who left by the back door.
Sit anywhere that isn't behind the counter. Behind the counter is where mistakes get buried.
Rum is rum. If it tastes of something else, that's the cup's fault and the cup's business.
Quiet night. I like quiet. Quiet means nobody is bleeding on the floorboards.
The ruins are a fine landlord. No rent, no questions, and the roof never gets fixed.
Ask me who drinks here and I say everyone. Ask me who pays and I say most.
A drunk will tell you anything. A sober man will tell you the same thing for a price. I just pour.
Everybody passes through the Hub eventually. That's why nobody wanted to keep it.
I hear the Holy Nation wants the walls back. Funny. They aren't the ones sweeping them.
Three coats on the peg and one of them is not coming back. I will sell it by morning.
There are shadows in this town that were here before the bar. They tip well, so I don't ask.
Lately the road brings more outlanders than customers. Outlanders look at the menu and leave.
Two thousand a day to guard your skin. Not a cat less, and I won't smile for it either.
Hired a squad to walk me to Stack once. They walked me. That's all the contract said.
Guild rules: you pay, we fight, we don't ask what was in the crate. Mostly we don't ask.
The work dries up when the war goes quiet. Then I miss the war. Strange thing to say.
Every employer says it will be an easy job. I have a scar for each time that was true.
Contracts are simple. Dying is simpler. I keep my contracts short.
Dust Bandits on the north road, starvers on the east. Pick which one you would rather lose to.
I counted four caravans this month. Three arrived. Ask the fourth how the guards were.
The Border Zone eats more boots than blades. Walk it in good boots or don't walk it.
Squad of Shek crossed the plain last week. Left the traders alone. I don't trust a quiet Shek.
That tower at the edge of the Hub takes a cut from anything that passes. Pay it or go around.
We turned down a job to escort a cart to Squin. The man would not say what was under the tarp.
I keep the peace for a fee. The peace is cheap. It's the people who cost.
Everybody comes to the Hounds when they have burned something. Few come back to say thanks.
Hash goes north, cats come south. I like how that sounds. It isn't always how it goes.
People think I'm soft because I make deals. A deal is just a fight you win with your mouth.
Sit down, have a cup. If you're here to be forgiven, you can start with the tab.
Big Grim built the Hounds out of swamp mud. The rest of us just carry the goods. Don't tell the Ninjas.
Walked from the Skinner's Roam on these. Feel them. No, don't feel them.
I've been looking for work since the last war. Wars end.
Left one pair of boots in a bandit's stomach.
I can fix a roof, shoe a bull, and count to a thousand. Nobody here needs any of it.
My feet hurt in places feet shouldn't have. Anyone know a surgeon who works for stew?
Slept in a ditch with a goat last night. The goat complained about me, not the other way.
A man told me the Holy Nation has fallen. Another told me it's bigger than ever.
People say the cannibals have a capital now. A real one, with a throne. I laughed.
I heard the Empire is run by one man who never leaves a tower. Sounds dull.
The Shek sacked this place once. You can still tell. The ruins have a certain look of being sorry.
Somebody swears there's a town of nothing but skeletons in the black sands. Somebody drinks a lot.
I walked past a hive village once. They didn't hurt me. They didn't look at me either.
Ah, the cannibals, you know, they don't even chew. They swallow! I saw it! Well. Heard it.
I had fifty cats on me when I came in. Now I have a very good feeling about everything.
Bugmaster, right? Big one. Bigger than this bar. Probably. I was drunk, so no, not drunk then.
Blood Bandits ate my brother. Or married him. One of those. They had the same teeth, anyway.
Another round for the man who's going to stop talking right after this sentence.
I could take any one of you. Not today, I have a knee.
Last week a man asked me to step outside. I did. He didn't. We're both still here.
Break a table in this place and the Ninjas break your arm. I've seen the arm.
Nobody starts fights in here. They just wait for someone to finish theirs.
I once lost a fight to a stool. In my defence, the stool had help.
Whoever took my cup, I forgive you. Return it by noon and I forgive you more.
I don't hate anyone here. That's the secret. I'm too tired to hate anyone here.
Cactus rum is up again. Every time somebody shoots at a caravan it goes up a few cats.
Fuel is cheap in Stack and dear here. Guess who carries the difference.
A foodcube sells for less than the water you drink with it.
Iron plates go for three times what they cost where they're made. Nothing grows in the Zone but prices.
Never trust a stall that has no prices on it. That's where they decide what you're worth.
My margin is thin enough to cut yourself on. I have the scars to prove it.
I take the long way round every time now. Short roads have too many people waiting on them.
Lost a pack animal to a river raptor and a good mood to its owner. Both were the same afternoon.
Three weeks from Heng with a cart of spices and a head of lice. I'm a rich man in one of those.
The Shek will trade now, did you hear? They still don't smile when they count.
A guard asked to inspect my cart. I told him what was in it. He let me through.
Don't buy bread from a man who says it's fresh. Buy it from a man who's hungry.
Spent a month digging a ruin. It had one working lamp and a very rude spider.
The old machines aren't dead. They're sulking. There's a difference, and it's expensive.
Hand me any wire, any plate, any scrap with a number on it. I'll tell you what it used to be.
I dream of sealed doors. Always a sealed door and a tool I forgot to pack.
A Holy Nation man tried to buy my notes. For burning. I said the price was a lot of cats.
Everyone treats us like grave robbers. We're archivists with bad habits and worse luck.
I don't drink. I sit near those who do. It's the closest I come to a hobby.
The stool is the wrong shape for me. The stool and I have an understanding.
Somebody told me this place was once a fort. Somebody was wrong, or I forgot the wall.
I count the rivets in the ceiling. Three hundred and eleven. Yesterday it was three hundred and ten.
They stare. I let them. It's an old habit of mine, being stared at.
Humans say they're tired. I wonder what it's like to run down slowly.
A pile of scrap in the corner was once a man. Not much difference from the pile I keep in my bag.
I was told to find a repair table. I found a stool and some very polite thieves.
The Holy Nation burns what it doesn't understand. I'm what it doesn't understand.
Fresh grease would be welcome. A rumour would be welcome too.
I remember a hallway. I don't remember where it went. This bar isn't the hallway.
My joints sing in the rain. I thought for years it was the wind.
The warm things talk very fast here. The hive listens. It doesn't always understand.
Food is in the cup. Food is also in the cup next to it. The cups are the same.
This one is far from the hum. The hum is a good sound. The hum has no prices.
No-hives drink to forget a thing. The hive forgets without cups.
A man tried to touch this one's shell. The hive remembers hands.
Many chairs. Few of them fit. The hive stands. The hive is polite about it.
Flatskins serve rum in tin cups. A Shek would be insulted, if a Shek drank here.
I came for the trade. I stay for the quiet. Don't make the quiet shorter.
My father burned this town. I wonder if he sat in this chair first.
The old truces are thin, and my patience is thinner. Count that before you stare at my horns.
Stack sells me blades, and the Border Zone sells me poor excuses.
A Shek can sit among flatskins for one cup. A second is a challenge to the first.
Blessed... evening. Sorry. Good evening. I mean, evening. It's a very normal evening.
I'm just a farmer. Of stones. From, ah, a village. Near. Please don't ask which.
No, I have never held a Flame. Why would I ask what it weighs? Don't write that down.
A fine place. A sinner's place. Not that I think so. I think it's wonderful.
I came for the water. The water isn't holy. I checked.
Don't look at my hands. They aren't praying. They're just resting in a prayerful position.
If you lean a little to the left, you hear the Shek at the far table. I don't lean. I merely tilt.
Somebody said Phoenix, and half the room went quiet. That is the sort of thing one remembers.
I count the swords at each table. It's a harmless hobby. Don't tell anyone I counted.
A cup of anything, please. Nothing that makes me say what I think.
The bartender is a Ninja, a thief, or both. I'm only saying what everyone else is thinking.
I am here for the Flame and the cheap rum. One of those is a lie.
Spare a bite. One bite. I won't even chew loud.
I haven't eaten since the dust storm. The dust storm was last week.
Anyone leaving crumbs? I am a very patient floor.
I used to rob caravans. Now I rob my own pockets. They are empty. It stings.
Foodcube, fish bone, anything. I'm not proud.
My friend isn't asleep. He's just very hungry. Try him in the morning.
The Anti-Slavers would string us up if they caught us. Not that I sell anyone. I sell...
Don't look at the door. Everyone who looks at the door gets looked at.
I used to love this work. Now I check my shadow twice before I sit.
Anti-Slavers burned a camp last month. The papers are still blowing around in the sand.
I sleep in my armour. Cold, uncomfortable, but nobody has ever stabbed armour in its sleep.
Everybody loves freedom, right up until the food runs out.
Three hundred cats for a man's whole life. That's the price. Think on it over your cup.
I notice who pays for what. I notice who doesn't look away. The second list is shorter.
A collar leaves a pale ring for a year.
Not every chain is iron. Some are debts. Those are harder to cut.
Don't tell me your business. I'm just here for the rum and the exits.
I eat slowly, I sit near the wall, and I tip well. That's my entire plan.
Everything has a second owner. I just meet the third one. Cheaper that way, for them.
The tower has a good view of the road. The road has a good view of nothing.
People ask me for a discount. I give them a lesson in what that word costs.
Guards pretend to crack down. A few cats keep the pretence honest.
Don't carry anything shiny through a thief's town. It's rude to the locals.
I do not steal. I redistribute attention. The goods follow.
A bull outlives a bad road. The bull has told me this. Slowly.
Town folk sleep with walls and still lock the door. Walls are for those who forgot the sky.
Camp is a fire, a pot, and a rule: nobody steals the pot.
The wind changes at the old fort. I always say hello to it.
I trade goat milk for tools, tools for stories, stories for goat milk. A good circle.
Do not call me a beggar. I carry more than you do, I just carry it in my head.
They took my plot and my plough and left me the ground. The ground isn't worth much without them.
Bread is two days old. I'm three. The difference is clear to everyone but the baker.
The Empire taxes the harvest and the hunger both. Somehow the hunger pays better.
I'd plant here, if the ruins didn't keep falling on the rows.
A man with a hoe is a threat if he's angry enough. That's what the tax collector learned.
Plant when the rain allows, bury when the raiders do. A good cycle, if you don't mix them up.
Every wound is a story, and most of them end the same.
A splint and a stern word fix most things. The rest, I charge extra.
A man came in with a bolt in his thigh and asked if it would scar. It did. He lived.
People think I'm kind. I'm thrifty. A man who lives pays twice.
I stitched three Shek last week. They didn't wince.
Wash your hands. Nobody ever does. That's how I make my living.
Nobody in the Hub calls for the law.
I am off duty. That means I am armed in a bar. Do not read anything into it.
Station is three days north. The criminals know.
A cop in a lawless town has two jobs. Stay alive. Keep his tunic clean.
I drink alone and I drink slow. I watch the room. It isn't a habit, it's a diagnosis.
Bounties are good money here, if you can collect before somebody collects you.
The stew has bones in it. I asked what animal. The cook said, an animal.
Bread here's hard enough to build with.
Somebody left a fish on the counter two days ago. It's still there.
I ordered the special. They said the special was a warning, not a dish.
The rum is clean. The cup is not. Some choices are just that: choices.
Meat of the day, they said. The day wasn't specified.
My feet are two different sizes now. I'd complain, but they can't hear me anymore.
Rested one night in the ruins and a roof beam kept me company. A fine and frightening thing.
Four days on foot and I'm hungry for a chair more than a meal.
I bought boots in Stack. The sole is already apologising.
Never walk in new boots. I walked in new boots. I'll tell you how that ended if I can stand.
Walk enough in the Zone and you stop noticing the pain. You start noticing your knees instead.
I was robbed on the east road. Politely, too. He said please. Then he took the boots.
Lost my pack, my bull, and my afternoon. The afternoon was the one I missed most.
Some bandit stole a man's trousers last week. Not the cart. Not the purse. Trousers.
Caravan three days out is missing. Everyone says it will be fine.
I'm not saying the guard sold us out. I'm saying he's wearing a very nice belt.
They left me one boot. One. I walked here in the other's silence.
Dust blew in the whole night. I swept it out. In the morning it was back, with friends.
Smells like acid rain. You can tell by the way the old men start counting their fingers.
The wind in this place has opinions. Right now it has the opinion that I should leave.
Warm today. Which is a lie. The cold just went to get its coat.
Last storm took a wall. It didn't bother with the door.
A man at the next table says it will rain. A man always says it will rain. That man was right once.
This was a Holy Nation town. Then the Shek came. Then the Holy Nation came back. Then nobody wanted it.
Funny thing about the Hub. Everyone has owned it. No one has wanted it.
The walls have burn marks on the north side. Ask about them and every man tells a different war.
They call it the Hub because everything crosses here and nothing stays. I think it is a joke.
Somebody says the Shek razed it. Somebody says the Holy Nation did it to spite them. Somebody is paid either way.
There was a plan to rebuild, once. The plan is under that wall, with the rest of the rubble.
Stack is a half-day on the road. Better prices, worse company.
Squin has the Ninjas and the water. I don't trust either.
Mourn is down the road. I hear the bar has a Hound at the back. Everybody has a Hound.
Tiny Settlement isn't a settlement. It's a pile of walls and a goat.
Past the old Shek ruins the grass gets thin and the men get thinner.
The Rebel Base is a short walk. It has the same barman as here. He's faster than he looks.
The black tower in the Zone belongs to people who dress like night. They want money for passing it.
If a ninja asks for a toll, give it. If he asks twice, give it faster.
I didn't pay once. I don't walk that road anymore, and my knee doesn't forgive the lesson.
They don't take everything. Just enough that you remember to bring a little extra next time.
Safe road, safe tax. The tower doesn't like it when you call it a racket.
A friend refused the toll. The tower sent a note. The note was his own coat.
The Holy Nation and the Shek have been killing each other for generations. I make my living between funerals.
I heard the Cities want the Holy Nation gone. I heard the Cities are too busy counting.
War is a loud thing, and the Hub is a quiet place.
Every few years someone says the war is over. Then the war says otherwise.
They say a Phoenix rules the Holy Nation. They also say the Lords rule him.
A Shek told me he would die gladly in some gateway. I told him I'd rather die in a chair.
The cannibals have a capital now. A real one. I wish I could say that was a rumour.
Whenever the wind blows from the south-east, the old men lock their doors. They won't say why.
I know a man who was eaten. He tells the story quite well, considering.
Never trade with someone who licks his lips. You will pay in extremities.
Cannibals don't hate you. That's the horror of it.
A hunter came through with a dog and a very long stare. I bought him a drink.
I heard the Emperor hasn't been seen in years. I also heard he's seen constantly.
A man in a good coat swore the nobles keep a skeleton or two as curios. A man in a worse coat disagreed.
Cities taxes are the real monster. Cannibals just want your arm.
Somebody says the Empire is just a second coming of something older. Everyone nods.
A noble came through once. He had four guards and a bad smell. I couldn't tell which was louder.
Out in the southwest, the laws aren't laws, just suggestions with fines.
The Holy Nation has ears here. I know because I've met the ears.
A priest passed through preaching purity. Left with a full purse.
I heard Phoenix can see a lie from three miles. That's probably an exaggeration of two and a half.
I don't say anything against the Flame while the room is full. Or empty.
The Holy Nation took a good man from the next table. Said it was a misunderstanding.
There are paladins in the east road. Heavy ones. They don't like to be asked about the weather.
The hive in the west is fine, I hear. Until someone takes their queen. Then it isn't fine.
I saw a drone buy a bowl of rice. Paid exact change.
Never argue with a soldier drone. They agree with you, then they stand in front of you, forever.
They say a prince in the south has no hive anymore. Poor lad.
Hivers don't drink. I have always wondered who they save the money for.
The folk in the Stack bar say the hive hums at night. I haven't heard it. I don't want to.
A man in the corner has a price on him that would buy this whole town.
Never stare at a poster longer than the man who posted it. That's how you end up on a poster.
A bounty hunter spent a month tracking a thief. The thief was in the next room, the whole time.
Dead bounties pay half. I pay attention to that, every time I meet a man I dislike.
My cousin turned in a bounty. He got paid. Now he drinks alone, and the bounty's friends drink with him.
I'd trade a good name for a good bounty. A good name doesn't keep the rain off.
My bull has a better pedigree than I do. He also has better manners, and a better sense of direction.
A man offered me three hundred for the bull. I told him the bull was not for sale. The bull agreed.
Never name an animal you plan to sell. That's the entire lesson of my life.
The wild dogs come at dusk. They don't bite. They stare.
Landbats up north took a whole herd last year. We lost the goats. The bats were fine.
River raptors will take a whole row of crops overnight. That's why I don't farm.
Put it on my tab. Somebody. My tab, the one that's long and has a face on it.
I've never been charged for a drink I didn't want. I've never wanted any other kind.
I tipped the barman once. He gave it back. I've been uneasy since.
Last time I paid for a round, nobody drank it. Strange. I was proud of my generosity.
The price of ale has gone up. The ale has gone down. I'd like the old ratio back.
Order something strong. The weak things here aren't safe.
Somebody patrols the north wall. Somebody else patrols the somebody. We're safe as can be.
The Shinobi in the tower watch the road. I watch the Shinobi. It's a very busy night.
No sleep till dawn. No dawn till sleep.
A strange squad rode past at midnight. They were quiet. Quiet is worse than loud.
Don't leave your pack on the floor. Not because of thieves. Because of rats.
The ruins make noises at night. The Ninjas say it's the wind.
Your pack smells of something the statutes don't like. Keep it closed in the Cities and we'll both be happier.
I'm not searching you. I'm merely reminding you that I could, and that the fine is two thousand.
Contraband carries a fee, and a signature, and an unpleasant afternoon. Which one do you prefer?
Citizens declare. Visitors declare louder. You, I notice, haven't declared at all.
Whatever is in that bag belongs in a ditch, or a ledger.
Cities law is not complicated. Do not carry what is forbidden. You appear to be studying the exceptions.
That's forbidden goods, and you're in my jurisdiction. Guards!
I know that cargo. Hold where you stand.
Hashish, or worse. I don't need a nose. I need witnesses. Gentlemen!
Stop there. Stop! The law has a very specific word for what you're carrying.
I don't see anything. I've never seen anything. The inspector can ask the wall.
Whatever you are carrying, do not wave it around here. I have a licence to keep.
A fine for the buyer, a fine for the seller, and a worse one for the man who stands near.
Business is business, friend. But some business has a very long arm.
The guards are never far and always bored. Don't give them a hobby.
There is darkness in your bag. I can smell it. Cast it into the fire or be cast with it.
The Flame has a list of forbidden things. You seem determined to carry every item on it.
Unclean goods, unclean company. Turn back, brother, before the Flame does it for you.
A pious man leaves that behind. A careless man leaves it in a ditch. A fool carries it past me.
The Holy Nation burns what it must. It would be a pity to include you in the pile.
I'll pray for the one who sold you that. For you, I'll pray quickly.
Heresy in a bag! Brothers, to me, this one carries forbidden things!
Seize that pack! Burn what is in it before it taints the street!
Contraband and heresy. I won't hold my tongue.
The Flame sees you and so do I. Hold, sinner!
You carry weakness in a sack, /FLATSKIN/. A Shek doesn't need it. We don't like it near us.
Whatever that is, it's a coward crutch. Take it somewhere I can't smell it.
I do not care what you chew or smoke. I care when it makes a fool of someone near me.
The Kingdom forbids that poison. I'd break it, but it would be a waste of a good strike.
A warrior takes a fight when he wants dreams.
Careful with that cargo. Some of my best clients have a taste for it.
I don't judge. I take a small percentage of whoever else does.
If you want to sell what is in that pack, there are three men in the next town with deep pockets.
Papers, stamps, and an honest face. That's all it takes to move what you're carrying. You have only one of those.
The law frowns on it. The law also frowns on me, and look how that turned out.
Whatever it is, I didn't see it, and nobody here will tell. Welcome to the wastes.
Bag looks heavy. Heavier than the average. Good for you. Just keep it away from the Holy Nation.
Contraband? That's just a word cops use. Out here it's a purchase.
I would offer to buy, but I am out of the right sort of cats. Try a fence.
Keep it out of sight and nobody will mind. Wave it around and somebody will.
Smells of a fine afternoon. Don't let the priests catch the scent.
Ah. A fellow with taste. If you're selling, talk to me. If you're buying, talk to me louder.
The empire calls it illegal. The empire also calls itself clean. Both are wrong, and both pay.
Hash goes north, cats come south. You look like you're heading in a direction.
I can smell that from here, friend. Nice.
Careful with the Cities border. They're quite protective about what they make themselves.
That is a heavy bag. That is a very heavy bag. Mind who sees it.
Something in there's worth a fight. I just can't tell what.
A bag like that draws eyes.
You carry like a man with something to lose. Careful with that.
Whatever it is, the Holy Nation would kill for it.
Friend, whatever that is, nobody told me. Walk on, we're fine.
You carry trouble in your pack, but you carry it among friends.
If the law asks, you were never here. If the law pays, you were.
I have a blind eye for people I like. Mind that I don't have two.
A machine in the shape of a man. The Lord of Light would not recognise you. Neither do I.
Move on, abomination. I haven't decided yet whether the Flame would be wasted on you.
Your kind has no soul to save. Don't look at me as if you could ask for one.
Walk with the dead if you must. Do it elsewhere, where the faithful can't see.
Do you sleep? Do you pray? No? Then there's nothing left to say to you.
Machine! The Flame was made for this. Brothers, the abomination walks!
I'll break you down into little pieces and bury each in a different place.
Hollow thing, we do not suffer your kind. Run now and perhaps you will rust slowly.
No soul. No mercy. No rust left in you when we are done.
Your face is a mask over a lie. The Flame will see the lie burn.
Skeleton. You walk like one who has fought a long time.
I heard your kind cannot die properly. A pity. A good death is the only gift we have.
Metal bones, no flesh to cut. A hard thing to fight. An easy thing to respect.
I won't strike a skeleton for sport. But don't make me wonder how loud you fall.
You have the stillness of a warrior and none of the blood. Strange. I do not hate it.
Is that an original build? The joints, the plating... Do you have papers? Of course you don't.
Forgive me. I have read about your kind for years. The reading didn't do you justice.
You must have been under a mountain for a thousand years. Please tell me you remember some of it.
A skeleton. Alive. Walking. I may need to sit down, and then write all of this down.
There is a repair kit in my pack that is older than I am. It is yours if you ask.
Do you mind if I measure your arm? For science. And, yes, for greed, a little.
Another of us, still walking. I count ten who aren't.
You carry yourself well. Better than the broken ones we pass in the sand.
The sun is a bad idea. You know it, I know it. Walk in the shade of an old wall with me.
I would say it is good to see you. I do not know what I am saying.
Your joints click. So do mine. It's a kind of conversation.
You're one of us. I know the shape. Try not to be one of the ones who break.
Metal bones, steady feet. Do you remember anything older than the road?
I don't know your model. I know your gait. We're the same kind of tired.
Greetings. If you find an old repair kit, remember the ones who wait.
The humans are staring at you. I was staring at you. Please, don't mind either of us.
A skeleton. Fine. Keep to the road and stay clear of the nobles. Some of them collect your kind.
Keep away from the noble houses. Some of the gentry like to hunt what they find walking about.
I have no quarrel with your kind. I have a quarrel with certain houses that keep trophy rooms.
Papers? No. Machines don't carry papers. Pity. It would make this simpler.
You're tall, and exactly what slavers and nobles look for.
Oi, tin can. If you drink, you leak. If you leak, it goes on the floor.
Fine armour you have there. Is it armour, or is it you? Hard to tell.
Is it true you don't eat? I'd pay to see you try the stew.
You're likely the only one for miles who isn't hungry. I wonder if that makes you happier.
A skeleton on the road. Next you'll tell me the rain is polite.
Watch your joints around Ninjas and slavers. They pay well for scrap, and they aren't particular.
A skeleton in the open. Noble houses pay well for a tall one. I'm only mentioning it.
I do not buy skeletons. I know three men who do. I know where they are.
Quite the specimen. Don't run. I'd hate to ruin a good piece of merchandise.
How much do you weigh? Not that I'm asking. Not that it matters.
The metal one moves like the hive moves. Not the same. Close enough.
No-hive and not flesh. The hive notes this. The hive doesn't mind.
Metal and quiet. Compatible with the hum. Compatible, yes.
The no-hive with iron bones. The hive has no word for you. The hive will make one.
That arm isn't yours. Nor that leg. Do you ask the Flame's permission for everything you replace?
Wires where the Lord of Light gave you bone. I will pray for the part that is still real.
A man made of tools. The Holy Nation would sooner you burned than rusted.
I see the shine of metal under that sleeve. Take it off, or take yourself off.
Machine parts on a living man. The priests will have words with you, and the paladins will have more.

say: There it is, the cursed limb!
Half a man, half a lie. The Flame will see which half lasts!
You carry abominations on your body. We will carry you to the fire.
Metal in the flesh! Heretic! The Lord of Light shall not suffer it!

say: Who made that arm? I want to know. I want to know right now.
The wiring on that limb is a work of art. The pain it took to install isn't. How are you managing?
I have spares, if you need. Don't mention the price. We'll both be embarrassed.
A man who wears the old craft. Respect. And a drink, if you have the time.
You're carrying a piece of history on your shoulder. Treat it with the dignity of a museum.

say: A flatskin with an iron hand. Brave, or foolish. It's hard to tell from where I stand.
Your arm is not flesh, but it grips like something that wants to live.
Iron where the flesh was lost. A warrior would call that honest.
Do you feel the blow when it lands? No? Then you are wasting the lesson.
I wouldn't take it from you. Taking is for men who can't earn. Show me you can earn it.

say: Fine workmanship, that limb. Where did you get it? No. Don't tell me.
I have a cousin who lost a leg in the Red Rebellion. He would have paid anything for what you wear.
Don't walk near the nobles with that. They have a certain interest in your kind of machinery.
A metal limb costs a small estate. You either stole it or earned it. I'll assume the better.
I don't stare. I only observe. Observe now, how much I'd pay for a look at your wrist.

say: The no-hive carries a machine limb. The hive notes it. The hive doesn't say more.
Metal limb. It replaced something. The hive understands replacement.
A no-hive with a metal limb. The hive is curious. The hive won't ask.
A good limb. Strong. A good limb works as one body.

say: That limb alone would buy my cart. Do not look at me like that. I am only valuing it.
I know a noble who pays double for a man with an iron arm. Triple, if he's still breathing.
A cripple with a prize. Careful, friend. Prizes get noticed by the wrong people.
Is it detachable? Don't answer that. I have too many ideas already.
Hell of an arm. Does it hit harder? Or does it just hit sooner?
I'd trade a good ear for a limb like that. A good ear and a bad knee.
Is that metal? Real metal? Lost a hand once. Wish I had met you then.
Don't take it off in public. People will want to touch it.
Priests will have your head for that. Priests have a hobby of that sort of thing.
That limb must have a story. Keep it. It's worth more than the arm.
You look like a fence post that learned to walk. Eat something, before you fall in the soup.
A bowl of stew costs a few cats, a bad bowl costs less. Don't die before the bad bowl.
I've seen the look. Hunger first takes the colour out of the eyes, then the manners.
Sit. Eat what I can spare. Pay later. Or never. I have a bad memory for hungry friends.
You're one of the walking hungry. They fill the wastes these days. I wish there were a cure.
Hunger is the first test of the faithful. The Flame feeds those who endure it, brother.
Go to a Holy farm and beg a bowl. They give it to the humble.
The Lord of Light has set a feast for the righteous, though perhaps not today.
A fast is a prayer with an empty belly.
I'd give you bread, but your faith isn't my business, nor your mouth.
You look half-dead, citizen. In the Cities, hunger is an offence. Eat before I notice.
Starving in public is bad manners. Starving in front of the law is worse.
Poverty is a crime, and hunger is its accomplice. Please correct both.
There's a soup line in most cities. Find it, and don't mention my name.
You're blocking the road, hungry as a dog. Move on, and mind your tone.
A hungry warrior is a dangerous one. A hungry flatskin is a sad thing. Which are you?
Eat, and live to fight. Or starve, and be forgotten. The Kingdom is plain on this.
I have starved with the best of them. It doesn't improve the character.
Do not beg. A Shek would sooner die. Take it as a sign of health.
A Shek keeps meat for the road. I do not offer it.
Brother, you're skin and bone. We're all skin and bone. Share, and we'll share with you.
Do you have any food? Any? Tell the truth. I'll know if you lie.
You look as bad as I feel. Maybe we should join forces. Maybe we should starve in company.
I know the look, friend. I saw it in the mirror before I broke it.
There was a time I was proud. Then there was a time I was hungry. Don't choose the second.
Hungry, hm? Hunger makes cooperative stock. Not that I'm suggesting anything.
A meal and a roof are easy things to promise. That's where my business starts.
Don't worry. A starved man sells for less, but he keeps quiet.
I'll tell you where to find food. I'll also tell you a place where they pay for hands. Interested?
You are wasting away. There is bread in my pack. Take it. No payment.
Feed yourself first. The rest of the world can wait for a plump man.
Pale lips, hollow cheeks. I know that hunger.
Slowly, now. Eating fast hurts after a long fast. I learned that the hard way.
The no-hive is hungry. The hive has food. The hive doesn't share with those who aren't hive.
Hunger is a loud thing. The hive hears it.
A thin one. The hive had a thin one once. The hive doesn't talk about that one.
You're the hungry kind. I envy and pity you.
I don't know hunger. I see it on the faces I pass.
Please eat. I do not know how much it hurts, but it looks like a lot.
That leg is wrong. Don't argue, I can see it. Sit somewhere, anywhere, and splint it.
You're limping like a dropped plate. A splint is a few cats. A cripple's life costs more.
I've seen worse and I've buried worse. Which are you going to be?
My uncle walked on a broken leg for a year. He walked in a very small circle.
Use a stick, use a friend, use a bull. Just stop using that leg.
A broken leg is a lesson. Take it, and walk again, or be left behind. The Kingdom has no pity.
Don't look at me for help. Help is for those who can't help themselves. Which are you?
I broke a leg once, a horn twice. I did not complain. I did not rest, either.
Crawl, then. A Shek has crawled further.
The Lord of Light tests us in the bones. Go to a healer, or pray, or both, but go.
A cracked leg is a poor pilgrim's burden. I would carry you if you were one of ours.
Don't rely on the Flame for a splint. Rely on cloth and a straight stick.
Bones heal. Sins don't. Be glad it's only a leg.
Move off the road with that leg. We have enough obstructions without adding another.
Cripples aren't permitted in the city streets without papers. I didn't write the rule.
Find a medic before the leg decides for you. Don't tell them I sent you, they gossip.
A broken leg and a broken purse. I recognise the type, and I pity the combination.
That leg slows you. That leg also makes you easy.
Broken, aren't you? What a shame. For you, I mean. For us, it's a very good afternoon.
Can you run? No? Then don't make me work for this.
A cripple on the road is a gift. Let me say thank you for that gift.
You're one cut from the ground. Get to a bed, or get to a healer. Not both.
I've seen men on their last legs. You're standing on yours, and it's shaking.
You look like a corpse who hasn't heard the news. Sit down before the news arrives.
Do not die in front of me. I have a very small tolerance for it today.
That's a lot of blood for one person. Keep it where it belongs.
A man that pale ought to be lying down. Get yourself wrapped up.
You stand when you should fall. A warrior's mistake.
Half dead, yet walking. The Kingdom has songs about men like you, and they're all short.
Fall or stand, flatskin. The ground is not your enemy.
I won't finish you. That's a courtesy, not a kindness.
Look at you. Barely breathing. Barely standing. Barely worth the effort.
A good shove and you'll meet the ground. Should I shove? I'm asking nicely.
That's a lot of blood you aren't using. Let me hold it for you.
One more hit and you're mine. One more. I'll wait.
Brother, the Flame is near, and so is the grave.
The wounded find mercy in the Holy Nation. The wounded who are faithful, I should say.
Bleed, if you must, but bleed where the paladins won't trip over you.
I have a prayer and a clean rag. The prayer will not heal you. The rag might.
Whose chain is that? Not mine, not my business.
A servant with shackles. Fine. The Cities have a law for that, and a very long list of exceptions.
I'd ask who owns you, but I wouldn't like the answer to be a noble.
Don't make eye contact with the guards. They see a collar, they see a stamp.
You have the look of a man who has been very busy and very unpaid.
That one belongs to someone. I know the brand. Get him to a station before I get ideas.
A runaway or a loan? I can't tell. Fortunately, I can charge for both.
Looks like decent stock. A bit of rust on the manners.
I hope you have your papers. Otherwise the three of us will have an awkward conversation.
The chain is a mercy to a heretic. It keeps the hands busy and the soul quiet.
A slave in the Holy Nation is a slave who hasn't yet found the Flame.
Don't look at me with those eyes. The Lord of Light sees all debts.
I have no quarrel with a chain. I have a quarrel with a chain on the wrong neck.
A chained man. The Kingdom keeps no chains. We keep honour, and the sword to defend it.
A man who lets himself be bound has little left to lose. Why does he walk?
I would cut that chain if it were mine. It is not. Hence I do nothing, as is the proper custom.
The weak get collars. The strong get names. Which will you be, flatskin?
That chain doesn't belong on you. Hold on. We'll find a key, or an axe, or both.
Stay near me. The next time anyone asks, you're travelling with me. Nobody needs a better name than that.
I wore iron too. Don't look down. Look at the road. It's longer than the chain.
Your shackles won't outlast the week. I give you my word, and my word is good.
There are folk who will break that lock. Speak to the first one who doesn't look away.
Whose slave are you? Don't tell me. I don't want to know whose throat I might need to cut.
Iron is heavy. I know a man with a good file. He asks few questions, and answers fewer.
Everybody walks with someone's chain. Some of us just wear ours on the outside.
I'm not saying I'll help. I'm saying I won't stop you.
I know that brand. That one is mine, or somebody's. Hold still.
A runaway! Take him alive, or take him in several pieces, but take him.
You thought the wastes would hide you? Somebody always sells a runaway for a few cats.
There you are, little bird. The cage is warm, and it's waiting.
Papers or chains. You choose. I have both, and I'm not particular.
Runaway property is runaway property. I don't like it, but the statutes are the statutes.
Look, I didn't see you. If I had seen you I'd be required to do something, and I'm very tired.
A fugitive in plain sight. If I were you, I'd learn to blend, and to walk slower.
The slave houses post descriptions. You fit three of them. Get off the main road.
You made it out. Your hands are still shaking. Mine did too.
Welcome, friend. Nobody here will ask you to explain a scar. We have the same ones.
Keep going. Find food, find a door without a lock, find someone who asks your name and doesn't use it.
I know the stare. You're listening for footsteps behind you. There are none.
You ran from servitude. The Flame is tolerant, but the Flame also keeps a ledger.
A runaway. Run further, or kneel and be counted. Do not stand around in the open.
I will not call the guard. I am only a pilgrim. I am saying this out loud so you can hear it.
Escaped from your master? Your master's master may still call for you.
Those shackles are locked. I'm not asking. I'm merely counting the turns of the key.
A locked wrist on a free man. The key is somewhere, and so is the one who holds it.
You walk like a man who owes the world a very specific debt.
I know where the nearest file is. I won't mention it, but I know.
Nobody chains himself. Whoever did that to you has a reason, and you have a problem.
Locked up and out for a walk. That's somebody's inventory, and somebody will want it back.
I'd ask for the key, but I'd rather ask for the owner.
You look like you belong to me. I don't think you do. Not yet.
Those irons are good irons. It would be a shame to waste them on a man who walks free.
Don't say anything. Don't speak. Just walk with me until I find a key.
That lock is nothing. I have opened worse. I'll open it, if you let me.
Walk with me. I'll tell you when to stop.
You don't owe me a word. You only owe yourself the next step.
Caged and asked nothing. A hard way to see the world, from a box.
I don't know who put you in there, but I hope the lock is worth it.
A cage is a cage, and a man in one is always a little more honest.
You'll wish you had a view better than this. I have seen it, from outside.
A live delivery. Good. The station pays on arrival, and the paperwork is only a morning.
Hand him over at the desk and ask for the receipt. It is a surprise how often people forget the receipt.
Is that the one on the poster? You carried him in. Not bad.
The law approves. The law also warns you to watch his hands, and his friends.
A prisoner and a poster. Well done. Watch your back on the way out.
A bounty on your shoulder. Don't stop here, friend. His friends may be looking for him.
You carry a man worth money. And a fool to carry him in the open.
Bounty hunters. Always the same face. Pale. Greedy.
He doesn't look worth the weight. But I suppose the weight is the point.
A live one is worth more than a dead one. That's the first rule.
A sinner in hand. The Flame is pleased with those who bring them in.
If that one is a heretic, bring him to the pyre. If he's a thief, bring him to the magistrate. If neither, bring him home.
Carry him gently. The Flame punishes carelessness with the same fervour as crime.
I would help you carry him. I would not help you ask where.
A corpse on your back. Who was he? Let me guess: expensive.
Dead men pay half. A rule older than the Cities. Don't argue with it.
He bleeds on your boots. That's a very personal kind of work.
The vultures will want a word about that. They won't get one.
Whoever he was, he's lighter now. That's a mercy, I suppose.
That smell isn't pleasant. That smell is a kind of paycheque.
You kill, and you carry. A hunter. Not a warrior.
He fell well, I hope. Not in his sleep.
A kill for coin. The Kingdom does not praise it. The Kingdom does not blame it either.
Carry him elsewhere. We don't mourn the ones who fall to mercenaries.
A body. If he was a sinner, he has already been judged. If not, may the Flame show mercy.
The dead are not mine to pass judgement on. Take him to the registry, quietly.
I'll say a word for the departed. Not for the killer. The killer has his own account to settle.
Hard work, bringing them in. The Lord of Light knows its worth.
Fresh stock, and still warm. You have an eye for it, friend. Where did you find him?
Beaten, bound and carried. A fine trade. I know three buyers who would take that off your hands.
I give twice what the stations do and ask only a quarter of the questions.
Bring him to a market soon, or I'll meet you on the road with a better offer.
Don't drop him. He's worth more whole than in parts, though I'd pay for either.
Put him down. Put him down now, or I'll take him from your hands and your hands from your arms.
A slaver carrying a body! Don't look away. Look at what you are.
You may wear a different coat, but I know the walk.
I won't let you sell that man. I'd sooner sell you.
A slave in transit. Fine. Take the back roads and keep out of sight.
Hm. I see a man with a sack and a conscience. I only wonder which will break first.
Statutes tolerate it. Neighbours don't. Choose your path, and your hour.
If you're selling, pick a quiet hour and a quiet buyer. I didn't say it.
The Flame has a use for every heretic. Whether it's a collar or a pyre, I don't decide.
Don't drag him past the faithful. Take the back way, with the rest of the cargo.
I would not carry a man I did not hate. Do you hate him? That is the real question.
You break a man's back for coin. I break my own in prayer.
Whose is that? Never mind. I don't want to know. Just don't let him wake near me.
Sell him in the next town. Sell him fast. Sell him far from anyone who knew him.
A body on your shoulder, a coin in your eye. You're in the right trade.
Every slave starts as a free man. It's only a matter of who carries him.
A modest bounty on a modest face. Pay it before it grows.
A small matter, but a matter. Settle at the station or I settle it for you.
A petty crime, not a hanging offence. Pay up, and I forget I saw you.
You have a name on a list. It's a short list. Don't make it longer.
The fines for that aren't severe. The fines for ignoring it are.
That bounty is a serious sum. I'm an honest man, and it's a very serious sum.
I know your face from the notice. Someone will make a good living from you. I'd rather it were me.
You're worth more as a headline than as a wage. Come quietly, and I won't make a speech.
A bounty like that doesn't come from a clerical error.
Stop. Don't run. I'd hate to chase someone worth this much, in this dust.
A price like that's a declaration of war. Guards!
I know that face from the notice. Seize them, and send word to the noble houses.
Fifteen thousand and more. You've made enemies in places that count.
Stop, in the name of the Cities. You're wanted, in a very large way.
A sin recorded. A small one. The Flame is patient, but not endlessly.
You have a mark in the ledger. Settle it, brother, and the ledger is forgotten.
A fine for a fault. The Holy Nation prefers repentance to punishment.
Your name is on a list. Not the worst one. Walk lightly.
A great sin, written in gold. The Holy Nation doesn't forgive that quickly.
You are marked, heretic. The ones who mark you do not forget.
The Flame has you in its sight. It won't look away.
I know your price. I wonder if the faithful will wait for the pyre.
The name from the great notice! Brothers, the Flame has delivered the unclean to us!
A bounty to pay for a church. Seize them! Seize them, and send for the paladins!
I have prayed for this. Don't move, sinner. Don't so much as bless yourself.
The sin of this one stinks to the sky. To arms, all of you!
/FLATSKIN/ law has marked you. /FLATSKIN/ law means little to a Shek.
A small price on your head. A Shek would take it as an insult.
I do not hunt for coin. But I would watch my back, if I were you.
A great price on you. Whoever put it there thought highly of your value, or little of your skill.
I have heard of you. The Kingdom hasn't decided what to do. I have, but I'll keep it quiet.
A man with that price walks like a king or a corpse. Which will you be, flatskin?
Someone wants you dead. That is a good start. It is not a recommendation.
You're on a list I own a copy of. Don't take it personally. Don't take it at all.
I've seen your face on a poster. The poster flatters you.
A bounty means someone thinks you're worth the trouble.
A price on you, friend, and I'm a patient hunter. Surrender, or pay the price in kind.
I don't need to fight. I only need to find the right moment.
We haven't met, but I know your name from three different notices.
A price on your head. A small one. Out here that's a good afternoon wage.
You have a price. It's a small price. Don't be insulted. I have a smaller one.
Wanted for something petty. Good. Petty is the best kind.
I don't do the law's work. I do my own. Today my own doesn't include you.
Five thousand and more. You did something big, or somebody important got very mad.
I could use five thousand. I could also use a long life. Today I choose the life.
Careful, friend. Every drunk with a nose for coin can read a number.
You are worth a house in a decent town. Sleep with one eye open.
That's a good bounty. A great bounty.
Fifteen thousand cats and more. If you aren't a monster, you're doing a convincing impression.
With a price like that, I'd be a king. Or a corpse. Or both, in quick order.
Don't stand near me. I'd hate to be killed by mistake.
That bounty is worth half the wastes. The other half is trying to decide how to take it.
Whoever you crossed, they have a very good memory and a very good purse.
A rich bounty on a free man. That's a thing I know how to handle.
A price like that makes a man valuable. Come, let me help you meet the ones who posted it.
Don't run. I'd hate to waste a good price on a short chase.
Wanted, on a notice, in ink. I do love it when the paperwork is already done.
A purse like that has a way of finding doors. Allow me to open one for you, citizen.
The most distinguished traveller I've seen this week! Or month. Or lifetime. I'm not good at estimating.
You carry a fortune and no guards. Either you're very brave or very well protected.
I have a cousin who sells fine cloth. I have a cousin who sells fine swords.
The Cities welcome all who bring their cats in good faith.
Wealth speaks. I only hope it doesn't shout in the wrong street.
You hum with cats. I can hear them from here. Sweet.
A man with that much money doesn't need all of it.
I'm only looking. Looking is free.
You have the walk of a man with a very full purse and a very empty escort.
How many cats? A guess is enough. A hundred would do me. A thousand would be rude.
The Holy Nation accepts tithes in all forms. Particularly in coin, particularly in quantity.
A man who carries that much might spare a little for the Flame.
Great wealth is a burden on the soul. The Church would be delighted to lighten it.
The Lord of Light favours the generous. He doesn't mention it in public.
You jingle like a goat with bells. Do you think that makes you strong?
Cats are for flatskins. A warrior carries a blade, and eats what it brings.
I don't envy gold. Gold is a sleep that comes too easy.
Rich and slow, a combination I have learned to hunt.
That purse is loud, friend. Keep it quiet or somebody will keep it for you.
Lunch is on you. Dinner is on you. Breakfast, well, we'll see how you feel.
A rich man out here's either a fool, a prince, or a bait. Which are you?
I know a very good tailor, a very good surgeon, and a very good grave.
I'm not going to mug you. I'm going to be your friend. That's more expensive.
Walk in the middle of the road. Sleep with one eye open. Tip everyone well.
That purse is a little heavy for the road. May I offer to lighten it, as a service?
I'd never lift a thing from you. I would, however, advise you to be careful on the road.
The weight of that purse. I can feel it from here. It isn't good for the spine.
A man carrying that much is either lucky or watched.
Penniless in the Cities. A near-crime, you understand. Do keep to the side roads.
No cats, no business, no excuse. Move along, there's a ditch further down.
Poverty is catching. Please stand somewhere else.
I would offer you a coin. I would also offer you a lecture.
You're one bad week from the gutter. You are, I suspect, in the bad week.
Not a cat in that purse, is there? I know the look. I wore it for years.
Empty pockets and a long road. The Cities are hard on both.
I'd give you bread, but my own is counted. Try the temple steps, or the tavern kitchen.
A bad week can last a year. Don't let it become your trade.
Keep your head up. Poor is common here. Poor and proud is rare, and gets noticed.
Not a cat to your name? Then you're the only one for miles who can't be robbed.
Broke. Honest broke, I can tell. Honest broke is rare. I pay it respect.
Come sit with me a while, friend. A beggar and a thief have more in common than they admit.
You're one of those who have nothing to lose. That's a dangerous kind of man.
Nothing in the purse, and a hole in your boot. I'd say I feel sorry for you, but I'm too tired.
The humble are blessed. You must be near sainthood by now.
If you have no coin, give the Flame your labour.
Poverty is a test. Yours seems to be a very thorough one.
Alms are for the faithful. Are you faithful? I only ask because the cup is small.
That armour was sanctified for someone better. Take it off, or I take it off you.
A thief in holy plate. The Flame has an appetite for that sort of fraud.
You wear our colours as a costume. The Holy Nation does not enjoy theatre.
That chest plate has a history, heretic.
I know the weight of that armour. You carry it like a stolen coat.
Where did you get that uniform? No, wait. Don't answer. The answer is a crime.
Wearing a samurai's colours without a samurai's right is called theft here.
That armour is registered. Registered to someone who isn't you.
A costume, a stolen coat, or an honest mistake? I'm willing to believe the third.
Our markings on a flatskin's back. Do you wear them to honour us, or to mock us?
That isn't Shek blood. That isn't Shek armour. That's a Shek insult.
I will have those horns, those plates, and that confidence off your back.
You wear what a warrior won.
That isn't yours. I don't mind.
A borrowed shell. Some of us keep our own. You, I think, are keeping someone else's.
The armour doesn't fit your voice.
I know that plating. It wasn't made for you.
Those are another's colours. Wear them with care, or give them back.
The no-hive wears hive colours. The hive doesn't remember giving them.
This shell has an owner. The hive knows the owner. The hive waits for the owner.
A no-hive in our cloth. We're many.
The hive sees a false drone. The hive isn't angry.
Take it off, no-hive. It doesn't suit you.
No-hive wearing the hive. The hive does not forgive theft.
We know our own. You aren't ours.
The hive counts every drone. You're the one extra.
Borrowed colours, no-hive. The hive will take them back.
That cloth has a hive and it is not yours.
That's a stolen look. Whose throat did you cut for it?
You wear our colours, or something near them. I'd explain it to the boss, if I were you.
Don't pretend. I know a costume when I see one.
You look familiar. You look like a man who has done this before.
Nice armour. Is it yours or did you sew it from a dead man? Not my business.
Careful. People take that uniform personally, and not always from the right direction.
I've seen disguises before. Most of them are better than yours.
Wear what you want. Just don't wear it near the people who made it.
A horned beast walking a human road. The Lord of Light made you strong, and then forgot you.
I do not speak with beasts. I only watch them, and pray they pass.
Shek. Everyone fears you. Nobody respects you. Think on that.
We were at war with your kind before your grandfather's grandfather was born. I am still a little tired.
Your eyes are the colour of a war. Look elsewhere, I beg you.
A bug on the road. A thing without a soul. Don't touch the children.
You're a hive thing. You have a queen, and the Flame has a pyre.
I do not know how the hive prays, or if it does. I know that it does not pray to us.
A drone walking free. I would feel sorrier if I did not feel afraid.
The Holy Nation says your kind has no soul. I only say you have no business here.
A /FLATSKIN/, walking proud. Do you know where you are? Do you know what you are?
Smooth skin. Smooth hands. A smooth life.
You don't look weak. You look unfinished. We can work with that.
The Kingdom tolerates outsiders in the places it chooses. Do not mistake tolerance for welcome.
A /FLATSKIN/ who looks me in the eye. Good. That's where it starts.
I smell no fear on you. I smell dust and rum.
A bug man. Walking in the open. Where is your hive, bug man? Where is your queen?
The hive doesn't fight like warriors. It fights like weather. We know both and we respect only one.
Insects with a mind. I don't like it. I don't hate it either.
Keep walking, bug man. This ground isn't yours, but the day is young.
Warm one. No-hive. You carry too much noise. The hive doesn't like noise.
A no-hive speaks. The hive doesn't answer. It's the way of things.
The warm ones are many and shrill. The hive wonders if you ever tire of yourselves.
You smell of fire and cooked meat. The hive does not eat what it cannot name.
A man of flesh. You tire. You bleed. You're fortunate. I can't tell if you know it.
Humans age. It's the most interesting thing about you.
I have outlived four of your kind who stood just there. Their names are gone. I am sorry about that.
You're warm. I can feel it from three feet. It makes me think of something I can't name.
A Shek among us. Peace, friend. We trade, we don't fight. I say it for the benefit of everyone.
People get nervous around horns. Keep yours up and your temper down.
I have no quarrel with the Kingdom. I have a quarrel with the last Shek who haggled with me.
A warrior among traders is a strange thing. I mean no insult. I mean it as an observation.
A drone. Don't worry, we don't mind your kind. I mean, we don't mind hivers.
I don't mind your kind. I mind how my customers look at you.
The guards keep one hand near the blade. It isn't personal.
Welcome, welcome. Please don't stay long. Please don't frighten the others.
No blade, no bow, nothing. A brave way to travel.
Walking about with empty hands, friend. Brave, or lost.
You look like a man who has never been robbed. Lucky.
I don't need to threaten you. The road does that on its own.
Lost your sword, or lost your mind? Either way, mind the road.
No weapon. Either you're a fool or you're a very good fighter. I won't test it.
A man without a blade is a man who has made peace with something.
A Shek would never go barehanded. A Shek would also never go meekly.
I can see your fists. They are unconvincing.
A traveller without a sword. Rare. Respectable. Possibly foolish.
Good. You aren't armed. I like that. Keep it that way as long as you're in the Cities.
Unarmed out here? You're either a monk or a madman.
If anyone asks, I didn't tell you to buy a knife. Buy two.
No sword? Out here? Either you're mad or you have friends in the dark.
Walk around unarmed out here and the wastes will arm you.
A man without a blade. I'd say I feel sorry for him. But I'm out of that.
Buy a cudgel, at least. A cudgel isn't a weapon, it's a conversation.
I've seen kinder men get killed for less than an empty belt.
You walk without a blade. A pilgrim or a fool, and the Flame has plenty of both.
There is virtue in an empty hand. There is also a very short life.
Unarmed, unguarded, unafraid. Blessed, or doomed.
The Holy Nation approves of those who put down the sword. It does not protect them from those who take it up.
That is a lot of feet for one road. Whose army are you, friend?
A column of fighters and a quiet road. I'd say the road is losing the argument.
Don't count them. Just don't make them count you.
I have a family. I have a post to keep. Please don't make it a battlefield.
A company that big doesn't walk. It occupies.
You march like a warband. That is either an insult or a compliment. I am deciding which.
A good company. A strong company. Not as strong as a hundred Shek, but strong.
If you come in numbers, come in honour.
Do you count your men, or do you count what they have killed?
Crouching in the open. I'd be offended, but I admire the commitment.
You tread like a cat with a conscience. That's rare, and I don't trust it.
If you are going to steal, do it somewhere less crowded. I would hate to be an accessory.
Not bad. Not good. The footwork is fine. It is the face that gives it away.
You're creeping, stranger. Honest folk don't creep.
I see you crouching there. Stand up, and explain yourself.
A man who hides is a man with something to hide.
That isn't a walk. That's a plan. Whatever it is, don't plan it near me.
New face. Don't worry, we all started as one.
Never seen you before. Sit, rest, and don't be a story by morning.
A stranger. Strangers are either money or trouble. Which are you?
I'd remember that face. I don't. That's almost as interesting.
Fresh off the road, by the look of the boots. Welcome to whatever this is.
You again. Did you forget something, or are you just fond of the scenery?
Back already? The road was not kind, I hope.
Two visits in a day. Either you like us, or something chased you in.
I was just beginning to miss you. Not really. But I was thinking about it.
Hello again. Your debt is still on my mind. It isn't as fresh as it was.
I know you. A bit older, a bit thinner, a bit quicker to look at the door. How have you been?
A few days away, and the world got bigger. Did you notice?
Back from the road. The mud on your boots tells half the story. Tell me the other half.
I was starting to think the Zone had finished you. I'm glad to be wrong.
Where did you go? Don't tell me. I'm only making conversation.
Well, well. I thought you were dead. I had even picked out your boots.
You've been gone a long while. Longer than the rum has been in the barrel.
A face from before. Last I saw you, there was a wall there. Now there's a hole.
It has been a long time. The faces change.
Do I know you? Wait. Yes. You owe me a cup.
There you are! Come sit. Tell me which of my rumours were true.
A friend returns. We have missed you, in our own awkward fashion.
You look better than the rumours said.
I kept a place for you. I wouldn't let anyone near it. Not really. But I thought about it.
Welcome, welcome. Look, touch, ask. Buying is optional.
A new customer. My favourite kind. They haven't yet learned my prices.
Not from around here? Good. I have a special rate for strangers.
I know most of the faces in my shop. Yours is a first.
Back so soon? I only just restocked the thing you didn't buy.
Did I overcharge you? I do that sometimes. Tell me, I'll rethink my conscience.
You again. Come in. Browse. I'll pretend I'm not counting the crumbs you left.
Short memory, long pockets. A merchant's favourite combination.
Look who remembered where I keep the good stock. A while now, was it not?
I put your usual to one side. Then I sold it. Then I felt bad about it. Come, I have a replacement.
I've had three better customers since you left. None more interesting.
Welcome back. Prices have changed. Mostly in my favour. Don't blame me, blame the roads.
I thought you had gone for a better dealer. I'm glad I was wrong, or I'm not.
I recognise that coat. It has aged better than you have. What brings you back?
It has been a long time. My hair went grey. The shop lost a wall.
A long absence. I'd offer a discount. I'll offer a smile.
You were here before the roof was fixed. I remember because you mocked the roof.
Stranger. Papers, or a good excuse. Failing both, a very good smile.
I don't know your face. That makes you either a traveller or a problem.
New here? Keep your hands where I can see them, and your opinions where I can't.
A new face in the Cities. Behave, and it will be a pleasant stay.
You were here a moment ago. Forget something? Carrying something?
Back again. I have a sharp memory for repeating faces.
Twice in a morning. Suspicious, or just absent-minded. I'll assume the second.
You keep coming and going. I don't mind. I only like to record it.
I know your face. Not from a poster. Not yet.
It has been some time. I hope you've kept out of trouble. The trouble hasn't kept out of you.
Look who returns. The record says you left owing nothing.
A long while. Keep to the law. It has aged less than you have.
A stranger, and unblessed. The Lord of Light welcomes all who come in peace.
I don't know your face. May the Flame show me your heart.
A newcomer. Be careful where you step. The ground is holy in places you cannot see.
Peace, traveller. Kneel, if it pleases you. Stand, if it does not. Just do not do it loudly.
You have returned. The Flame brought you, or the road did. I can never tell which.
Again, pilgrim? You seek something. Ask, before the Flame loses patience.
I remember your face. It troubles me. It troubles everyone, in the end.
Back so quickly. A crisis of faith, or a crisis of boots?
A long time. The Flame has burned many since. I am pleased you were not among them.
I thought the road had taken you. The Flame has a long memory and a short temper.
You return. The Holy Nation does not forget, brother. It only waits.
Many have gone and few returned. I don't ask where you went.
A new /FLATSKIN/. Walk with your head up, and your hands visible.
I don't know you. I don't need to. State your purpose, then your name.
Strangers are tested. Pass the test. Fail it, and you won't remember it.
A fresh face on the Kingdom's road. Don't make it the last.
You again. Short memory or short temper?
Back? I have not finished forgetting you.
Twice in a day. Either you're brave or you're lost.
I know that stride. Walk on, quickly, before I develop an opinion.
A long absence. Did the world beat you? You look as if it did.
I remember you, /FLATSKIN/. You're still alive. That's a small honour.
Time passes. Blades rust. You, I see, didn't.
You walk a little straighter than before. Good. A warrior may yet be made.
I have just seen you. Or I have forgotten. Which is more likely?
Hello. Again. I'm fairly sure it's again.
You were just here. I counted my own rivets twice since.
Greetings. Your face is familiar. That's either a good sign or a faulty memory.
You're the one from before. I kept the memory. It's the only one I could afford.
A long time has passed. I don't know how long. It was longer than I wanted.
I remember your shape. Not your name. Your name was lost to me at the second sunrise.
You return. Few do. I'll write it down, in the part of my head that still holds writing.
The no-hive returns. The hive remembers. The hive remembers everything.
A face the hive has seen. The hive did not mind it then. The hive does not mind it now.
Absent, then present. The hive notes the pattern.
We saw you pass. We see you again. The road is a circle, we are told.
I've seen you before. I never forget a good asset.
Back, are you? I was only thinking of you. That's a little frightening, is it not?
A familiar face. Hold still. Let me remember what I paid for it.
Still free, I see. A small miracle. I wouldn't rely on it.
It burns the cloth first, then the skin. Cover up! Cover up, please, cover up!
I'm not made for weather that bites. Where's a roof? Any roof!
Do you hear that hiss? That's us. That's us being eaten, slowly.
My mother said never go outside when the sky turns that colour.
I'll drown in it. I'll melt in it. I'll do both, and not in that order.
A little acid, a little sting. I have felt worse from a bad tavern.
Keep walking. Rain has never stopped a good fighter. It only slows a coward.
If it burns, it's working. If it's working, I'm still alive.
Rain! Ha! Come at me, sky. I've seen your worst.
Pull your hood and move. Shelter is somewhere ahead. We'll find it together.
Cloth burns slower than skin. Wet cloth burns slower still. Keep your boots on, keep your head down.
Stone overhangs. Dead trees. Anywhere with a ceiling. The sky doesn't apologise.
It's the dust in the air, drawn up by the heat. In a day it will pass and the ground will smell of metal.
If you must walk in it, walk fast. Standing in acid is how people become cautionary tales.
Don't drink from any puddle that's now bubbling. That should go without saying. I'm saying it anyway.
It's raining on me! It stings! It stings a lot. Is that normal?
Why is the water angry? Did I do something to the water?
My arm smells like a hot pan. Is my arm a pan?
I opened my mouth to catch some. Don't do that. I'm telling you now, don't.
Boots, hat, skin. Skin isn't on the list of things I wanted wet.
HAHAHA! The sky wants a piece of me! Let it have an arm! I have two!
Dissolve me! Dissolve all of us! The soup of the world!
I can feel every drop. Every one. Ha ha ha, it's wonderful.
The clouds bleed on us. I bleed on them.
Burn, burn, rain! I'll wear the scars like medals!
The sky spits at us. A Shek spits back. We're on equal terms.
Pain is weather. Weather passes. We remain.
Wet armour, burning skin. A fine day to be Battle Born.
Let the sky try. It has not yet beaten the Kingdom.
The Lord of Light tests us with burning rain. Praise him. Praise him quickly, then run.
A holy cleansing, perhaps. Or merely weather. I can't tell, and I'm too wet to pray.
Under the cloth, brothers! The rain is a sign, but not a welcome one.
The sky burns the unworthy. I count myself among the soggy.
The rain doesn't mind me. I don't mind the rain. We have reached an understanding.
Humans scatter. I walk. It's the only time I feel ahead.
Water on steel. A sound I almost remember.
Everyone else is running. I decline to hurry. I enjoy the contrast.
The ground is chewing my boots. Chewing! This isn't a joke!
I swear my soles are melting. I can feel each toe. I have never felt each toe.
Find a rock. Find a plank. Find a friend with a back.
Burning feet, burning temper. Put both out, quickly.
Whoever made this land should have included shoes in the plan.
A stinging sole never stopped a fighter. Walk faster, that's all.
I have crossed worse. I don't remember where. But I remember it was worse.
Hop, if you must. Just don't stop.
The water bites. Out, out, out of it!
I wouldn't wade that if you paid me. Yes, I'm wading it. No one is paying me.
My legs. My poor legs. They're going to be a very sad colour tomorrow.
Fish used to live here. Now there's only a smell.
Cross it quickly, boots high, and say nothing rude about the water.
Alkali, sulphur, old waste. The stream is a sick thing. Don't drink, don't linger.
Dead water. A polite word for a poison that still looks like a river.
Wash after. Immediately. Cloth, boots, hands.
I'm on fire! Why am I on fire? I did nothing!
No no no no no. Water! Sand! A friend!
I can smell my own hair.
Please stop it burning. Please. I'll be good for the rest of my life.
Burning! Right. Roll, drop, curse, repeat.
I've been burned before. It never gets easier, but it gets quicker.
Stand back and let me slap it out. It's only a bit of fire.
Hot! Hot! Hot! But still standing.
I AM THE TORCH! I AM THE BEACON! LOOK AT ME!
Warm! Finally warm! Do you feel it too?
Let the flame take the sleeves! Let it take the lot! I never liked those sleeves!
Ha ha! The light! The beautiful, hungry light!
The Flame is merciful, but it isn't gentle. Put it out.
Burning, Lord of Light! Is this a blessing? It hurts like a punishment!
If this is a test, I fail it.
It's only fire. It's only fire. It's only fire.
The wind has turned. Dust will follow, then grit, then sand in every pocket you own.
A dry wind from the east. Nothing good rides it, but nothing deadly either.
Cover the nose and mouth with cloth. Trust me.
I can taste the desert in the air. It's a sour taste, like old coins.
The wind took my hat. The wind is a thief. I want the wind arrested.
Why does the air keep pushing me? Did I owe it something?
I have sand in my teeth. And my ears. And that other place.
Whoa. Whoa! I almost flew. I almost flew away. Do not tell anyone.
A good wind. It cleans the sky. It also cleans the pocket, so hold on to your purse.
The wind is talking. I only wish it would talk about something useful.
Wind from the south means dry. Wind from the north means trouble.
Keep your bull close and your hat closer.
The wind whistles through my ribs. It's a lovely tune. I won't tell anyone I like it.
Sand finds every joint. Every single one. I'll be a month cleaning it out.
I could pretend to be a flute. I choose not to.
I can't breathe! I can't breathe!
The air tastes like a coffin. Get me out of it!
It is in my lungs. It is in my head. It is in everything!
Why does it smell like a graveyard that's on fire?
Hold your breath, move upwind, and don't cough.
Heavier than air. Stay high, stay moving, stay calm.
The cloud will thin in a minute. Not in two.
Cover your face. I do not care with what.
A cough never killed a warrior. A cloud might.
Grit your teeth and walk through. It can't be longer than a hundred paces.
I'll hold my breath until the end of the world, if that's what it takes.
I don't breathe. I do, however, remember it. I'm sorry for those who do.
The cloud passes through me like a rumour.
A strange thing, being the one who is not poisoned. I do not know whether to feel lucky.
Gone. Clean gone. Well. Now I know how it feels.
I will walk again. Maybe not on that. But I will walk.
A leg is a small price for a long life.
Don't look at it. I don't want to see your face when you look at it.
My leg! My leg isn't where my leg was! Where's it?
I can't stand. I can't run. I can't do anything but scream. And I'm doing that.
Tell me it is still there. Tell me.
It hurts less than I thought. That's the frightening part.
Ha! Ha! One fewer to keep track of!
Bring me a replacement! Bring me a stick! Bring me a dog!
I always wanted to know how it felt. Now I know.
Hop, hop, hop. The world is smaller on one foot.
A leg is a leg. A warrior fights from his knees if he must.
The Kingdom doesn't weep for the lost.
A debt paid in meat. I regret nothing and I regret everything.
A spare part would be welcome. A spare part would be very welcome.
I'll find another. I always find another. That's the secret of my kind.
Please don't step on it.
An arm. Hm. I had two. Now I have one and a good story.
It hurts. Obviously. But so does everything.
One arm is enough to hold a blade. Two arms were a luxury.
It's gone! My arm! It was right here a moment ago!
I cannot hold anything now. Not a sword, not a cup, not a hand. A hand!
Will I bleed out? Tell me I won't. I don't want to bleed out in a ditch.
My arm. My arm. My arm. I'm only saying it so that it's true.
The Lord of Light takes what he will. I do not have the right to complain.
A sacrifice. A small one. A big one, actually. I think it was a big one.
May the Flame forgive whoever did this. May the Flame also arrive soon with bandages.
It's gone. I won't call it anything but what it is.
I give no curse for it. I give a promise: I'll remember.
A lost arm is a debt. Someone will pay it, in time.
I was beaten. I accept it. I only wish I had seen the blow.
The ground is a poor pillow, but an honest one. Where is my sword?
I won't take up arms again today. I have learned a lesson, and it was sore.
I fell on purpose. Don't look at me like that.
Anyone see who hit me? Good. Keep it that way. I have a few thoughts on revenge.
I could have stayed down longer. I chose not to. It was generous of me.
Concussion. Mild. Nausea. Moderate. Pride. Severe. Where did I put my boots?
Count the fingers. One, two, three. All here. All mine.
I'll remember who was standing over me. Everyone, in case I need to ask.
What happened? Did I win? I feel like I won. Why am I on the ground?
My head is making noises. It isn't supposed to do that.
Is it morning? It isn't morning. Why did I think it was morning?
I had a dream about bread. It was wonderful. Then someone hit me.
Am I dead? No. No, the pain says otherwise. Thank you, pain.
Please don't hit me again. I'll do anything. I'll do nothing. I'll do whatever you prefer.
I'll stay very small and very quiet.
Who was that? Were they angry? I think they were angry.
I was beaten. I'm alive. Both are lessons.
I'll rise, and I'll remember the one who struck me.
A warrior does not curse the ground. He studies it.
Down but not out. Come here, and I'll show you a second chance.
I felt that one. Now you feel mine.
Not yet! Not today! Not like this!
Is that all you have? Then I'll return the favour.
Oh, that tickled! Do it again!
Back from the dead! The dead are always hungry!
Aaaah, you made me angry. How wonderful for both of us.
I've been hit by worse. I have BEEN worse.
I'm up! I'm up! Please don't hit me while I'm standing!
Why is the fight still going? Did nobody tell it to stop?
I'm not ready. I was never ready. I'm just standing.
Stay away! Stay away! I'm armed!
Count the exits. Count the enemies. Subtract the ones I can outrun.
Up, assess, retreat or counter. In that order.
They think I'm beaten. Let them. It's a useful mistake.
The Flame hasn't finished with me yet!
I rise in the name of the Lord of Light!
No corpse of mine will lie in the dirt when the Flame has a use for it!
I fall, I rise. That's the whole of it.
A true Shek is never beaten.
Down? Hah. Down is just another way to look up at you.
My blood is Battle Born. It doesn't stay on the ground.
Hurt? Bleeding? Either way, mind the blood. Not on my boots, please.
Medics Guild. We mend what we're paid to mend. Ask for a price before you ask for a favour.
If you're carrying anyone who can't walk, I'd see them first. The rest can wait their turn.
Bandages, splints, stitches. No miracles. Those are sold elsewhere, at a worse rate.
Show me the wound. Don't tell me how it happened. I'd rather work without the story.
Back already? Either you healed fast or you broke something new.
We only just spoke. Try to leave it a day before you come back bleeding.
Back again. Do try to keep yourself in one piece this time.
You look no worse than last time. That isn't praise. It's a low standard.
Look who walked in under their own power. I had you down as a lesson in a ditch.
A while now. I don't keep charts, I keep faces. Yours I kept.
Still in one piece? I charge for pessimism, so I'll say nothing.
You look like you've had a busy season. Busy seasons are good for the guild.
Hello, stranger. If you have work, I have time. If you have coin, I have more time.
A new face. Good. The old ones tell the same stories. Tell me one that ends differently.
Peace on the road, traveller. We keep our heads down here, but we keep them friendly.
Stranger. I'm only a peasant. I know nothing, own nothing, and have opinions about both.
You aren't from this stretch. Keep to the paths and nobody will mind.
You again. Still alive. That makes you better at it than most.
Back, then. I wasn't worried. I was watching the road, in case I became worried.
Good to see you. Do not look so surprised. We do speak to those we have already met.
Same face, different dust on it. Stay a moment, if you want. Standing is free as well.
Look at you, back from the road. I thought the road had kept you.
A good while. The rumours grew in your absence. Which would you like to hear?
I remember your face. Less dust on it then. Tell me where it has been.
You have been gone long enough that I started telling people you were a story.
